newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares rebound as Wall Street rallies.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares rebound as Wall Street rallies.

text.p: Italian shares reversed early losses on Tuesday to rebound to a higher close on the back of early strength in Wall Street which fed through to most European bourses, but the mood in Italy remained largely cautious.
"We are simply watching other markets, and any buying interest is still very cautious," said one dealer.
Olivetti crashed nearly seven percent before recovering to end just slightly lower on worries over what surprises might emerge at preliminary 1996 results due late Wednesday.
The blue chip Mib30 ended 0.84 percent up at 18,635 while the all-share Mibtel rose 0.82 percent to 12,480.

Dealers said that the Milan market was following Wall Street which rose early on the back of higher T-bonds sparked by a slightly weaker than forecast increase in the U.S. fourth quarter Employment Cost Index.

Olivetti ended off 0.76 percent at 651.9 lire as analysts predicted that the company might report net losses of 900 billion lire or worse for 1996 as the company embarks on a series of write-downs and restructuring.
"This is a chance for the new management at Olivetti to clean up the balance sheet, so that net losses for 1996 could be very large," said one share dealer.
Other blue chips managed a firmer trend with ENI up 1.16 percent at 8,920 lire, and Fiat 0.65 percent ahead at 5,304 lire after a spate of profit taking on Monday.

Among the telecoms, STET was 3.26 percent firmer at 7,927 lire after industry minister Pier Luigi Bersani said the government may hold a golden share until full privatisation. TIM ended up 2.82 percent at 4,863 lire and Telecom Italia was up 2.58 percent firmer at 4,658 lire.
